papers.title: Synthesis of Sb(iii)-immobilized on nitrogen-doped mesoporous silica nanotubes for efficient and green preparation of pyrazolopyranopyrimidines: comprehensive characterization, green chemistry evaluation and computational antifungal profiling against 5TZ1.
papers.abstract: In this study, a novel heterogeneous nanocatalyst, Sb(iii) immobilized on nitrogen-doped mesoporous silica nanotubes (N-MSNTs/Sb(iii)), was successfully synthesized. This catalyst was then applied in a one-pot, four-component synthesis of pyrazolopyranopyrimidine derivatives via the condensation of ethyl acetoacetate, hydrazine hydrate, aromatic aldehydes, and barbituric/thiobarbituric acid. Comprehensive characterization using FT-IR, FE-SEM, EDS, HR-TEM, XRD, and BET/BJH analyses confirmed its structural features. Notably, HR-TEM revealed hollow nanotubular structures with an inner diameter o
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a novel heterogeneous nanocatalyst by immobilizing Sb(III) on nitrogen-doped mesoporous silica nanotubes and used it to catalyze a one-pot, four-component synthesis of pyrazolopyranopyrimidine derivatives. The catalyst was thoroughly characterized and evaluated for green chemistry metrics, and computational docking studies were performed to assess antifungal potential against the 5TZ1 protein target.

papers.title: Integrated experimental and computational evaluation of atractylenolide III from Tubipora musica for anticancer lead identification.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major global health challenge, with over 900,000 new cases annually and a pronounced male predominance. In pursuit of novel, low-toxicity therapeutics, this study isolated Atractylenolide III from the marine coral Tubipora musica and demonstrated measurable, dose-dependent cytotoxic activity against HepG2 liver cancer cells, achieving an IC50 value of 15.50 µg/mL and reducing cell viability to 25.0% at 25 µg/mL. To investigate potential molecular targets and propose hypothetical mechanism pathways, we employed a multi-layered computational strategy. Mol
papers.summary: This study isolated atractylenolide III from the marine coral Tubipora musica and showed it kills HepG2 liver cancer cells in a dose-dependent manner (IC50 = 15.50 µg/mL). Computational docking and network analyses were then used to propose hypothetical molecular targets and mechanisms underlying this anticancer activity.

papers.title: Gut Microbiota and Aldosterone Regulate Natriuretic Peptide B Expression to Drive Mitophagy and Metabolic Reprogramming in Sepsis-Like Model of Myocardial Injury.
papers.abstract: Myocardial injury is a major contributor to mortality in sepsis, yet the mechanisms underlying gut-heart communication in sepsis-induced myocardial injury remain insufficiently defined. Natriuretic peptide B (NPPB) is a cardiac stress-responsive gene, but its involvement in mitochondrial homeostasis and metabolic regulation is unclear. This study investigated how gut microbiota and aldosterone influence myocardial mitophagy and metabolic reprogramming through NPPB in sepsis-induced myocardial injury.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
papers.summary: This study investigates how gut microbiota and aldosterone regulate the cardiac stress gene NPPB (natriuretic peptide B) to influence mitophagy and metabolic reprogramming in a sepsis-like model of myocardial injury. The findings suggest a gut-heart communication axis in which microbial and hormonal signals converge on NPPB to drive mitochondrial quality control and metabolic shifts in the injured heart.

papers.title: Kinetic, computational, and phylogenetic characterization of PA2125 from Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1: A hydroxybenzaldehyde dehydrogenase of the newly defined ALDH33 family.
papers.abstract: PA2125 from Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 is annotated as an aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH), but its substrate specificity, catalytic properties, and phylogenetic family assignment had not been established. Here, we cloned the PA2125 gene, produced and purified the recombinant PA2125 protein, and combined extensive substrate screening and steady-state kinetic characterisation with molecular dockings, molecular dynamics simulations, and phylogenetic analysis. PA2125 preferred NAD⁺ over NADP⁺, and screening of 54 aldehydes revealed a narrow substrate range centred on substituted benzaldehydes, part
papers.summary: This study characterizes PA2125, a previously uncharacterized aldehyde dehydrogenase from Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1, showing it prefers NAD+ and acts on a narrow range of substituted benzaldehydes. Combining enzyme kinetics, molecular docking, molecular dynamics, and phylogenetics, the authors assign PA2125 to a newly defined ALDH33 family as a hydroxybenzaldehyde dehydrogenase.

papers.title: Cross-docking and redocking reveal distinct determinants of success in physics-based and AI-driven binding pose prediction in protein-ligand complexes.
papers.abstract: Protein-ligand pose prediction is central to structure-based drug discovery, yet the relative performance of physics-based and AI-driven methods under realistic cross-docking conditions remains insufficiently characterized. Here, we compare physics-based docking methods (AutoDock4, AutoDock Vina, and DOCK 6) with data-driven approaches, including the deep-learning model GNINA 1.3 and the diffusion-based frameworks AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, and DiffDock. Performance was evaluated using standardised redocking and cross-docking protocols across three Alzheimer's disease targets representing distinct
papers.summary: This study benchmarks physics-based docking tools (AutoDock4, AutoDock Vina, DOCK 6) against AI-driven pose predictors (GNINA 1.3, AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, DiffDock) using standardized redocking and cross-docking protocols on three Alzheimer's disease targets. The results show that physics-based and AI-driven methods succeed under different conditions, with distinct determinants of accuracy, highlighting that no single approach dominates across realistic cross-docking scenarios.

papers.title: Reversible homodimerization of a small leucine-rich proteoglycan PRELP modulates the interactions with TGFβ1 and IGFI-R.
papers.abstract: Small leucine-rich proteoglycans (SLRPs) are responsible for various biological functions via their multiple interactions with various proteins. Although some SLRPs form homodimers, it remains unclear how homodimerization affects the molecular functions of SLRPs. Herein, we report the molecular basis and functional significance of homodimerization of PRELP, which is a member of SLRP family. We used biophysical techniques to validate the premise that PRELP forms a reversible homodimer in a concentration-dependent manner. Because the spatial aggregation propensity (SAP) calculation indicated tha
papers.summary: This study shows that the small leucine-rich proteoglycan PRELP reversibly forms homodimers in a concentration-dependent manner, and that this dimerization modulates its interactions with TGFβ1 and IGFI-R. The authors use biophysical methods and spatial aggregation propensity calculations to characterize the molecular basis of this dimerization, suggesting a regulatory mechanism for PRELP's biological functions.

papers.title: Integrated Experimental and Computational Investigation of Azobenzenoid Derivatives Against Trypanosomatid: RNA Editing Ligase 1 as a Potential Molecular Target.
papers.abstract: Neglected tropical diseases caused by pathogenic protozoa, including Chagas Disease (etiological agent Trypanosoma cruzi) and leishmaniasis (etiological agent Leishmania spp.), are public health problems in many developing countries.
papers.summary: This study combines experimental and computational approaches to investigate azobenzenoid derivatives as potential inhibitors of RNA editing ligase 1 (REL1) in trypanosomatid parasites that cause Chagas disease and leishmaniasis. The work identifies REL1 as a promising molecular target and evaluates the compounds' binding and activity, suggesting a possible route toward new treatments for these neglected tropical diseases.

papers.title: A sustainable functional food ingredient from Saussurea involucrata cell culture alleviates atopic dermatitis-like inflammation via arachidonic acid metabolic remodeling.
papers.abstract: Nutritional interventions may complement established approaches for managing atopic dermatitis (AD). Here, we evaluated Saussurea involucrata cell culture (SIC), a sustainable functional-food material, in a DNCB-induced mouse model of AD-like inflammation. Chemical profiling established the phytochemical composition of SIC, and both topical and oral interventions improved macroscopic and histopathological outcomes. Under the tested conditions, the oral groups showed more consistent changes in systemic indices, providing the basis for subsequent mechanistic analyses. Integrated transcriptomic a
papers.summary: This study evaluates Saussurea involucrata cell culture (SIC), a sustainable functional food ingredient, in a DNCB-induced mouse model of atopic dermatitis. Both topical and oral SIC interventions improved macroscopic and histopathological outcomes, with oral administration showing more consistent systemic changes. Integrated transcriptomic analysis suggests the anti-inflammatory effects are mediated through remodeling of arachidonic acid metabolism.

papers.title: Cooling-induced aggregation in SARA-Modeled crude oils near oil-water interfaces: Molecular mechanisms of interplay among wax, asphaltene, and resin.
papers.abstract: Waxy crude oils under high water cut, low temperature pipeline transport conditions undergo complex gelation upon cooling, yet the interplay between asphaltene, resin, and wax in confined oil layers near oil-water interfaces remain poorly understood. Through molecular dynamics simulations of model crude oil systems with systematically varied SARA compositions, this study reveals the cooperative and competitive mechanisms among these three components. Asphaltene initiates wax crystallization by serving as heterogeneous nucleation sites, whereas resin promotes subsequent crystal growth and enhan
papers.journal: Journal of colloid and interface science
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how wax, asphaltene, and resin interact in crude oil near oil-water interfaces during cooling. It finds that asphaltene acts as nucleation sites for wax crystallization, while resin promotes crystal growth, revealing cooperative and competitive mechanisms among the three components. The work provides molecular-level insight into gelation in waxy crude oils under pipeline transport conditions.

papers.title: Mechanistic elucidation of Panax ginseng in improving atherosclerosis via multidimensional artificial intelligence computing coupled with experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Atherosclerosis (AS) is the core pathological foundation of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases, and its efficient prevention is pivotal to lowering related mortality and disability. Panax ginseng confers remarkable cardiovascular protection, whereas its anti-atherosclerotic efficacy and intrinsic mechanisms remain poorly elucidated, restricting its clinical translation. This study sought to decipher the mechanism underlying Panax ginseng mediated AS improvement via multidimensional artificial intelligence (AI) computation integrated with experimental validation.
papers.summary: This study combines multiple AI-based computational approaches with experimental validation to uncover how Panax ginseng improves atherosclerosis. The authors identify mechanistic pathways underlying the herb's cardiovascular protective effects, aiming to support its clinical translation for preventing cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease.

papers.title: Novel indole alkaloids from the flower buds of Panax vietnamensis var. fuscidiscus: Distribution in reproductive organs and integrated biological evaluation.
papers.abstract: While the chemical constituents of flower buds from several Panax species have been reported, the phytochemical profile of the flower buds of Vietnamese ginseng remains understudied, particularly alkaloids. This study aimed to characterize alkaloids from the flower buds of Panax vietnamensis var. fuscidiscus (PVF), investigate their distribution across reproductive plant parts, and their biological relevance.
papers.summary: This study characterizes novel indole alkaloids from the flower buds of Panax vietnamensis var. fuscidiscus, a previously understudied Vietnamese ginseng variety. The authors also examine how these alkaloids are distributed across different reproductive organs and evaluate their biological activities. The work expands the known phytochemical profile of Panax species and highlights reproductive tissues as a source of bioactive alkaloids.

papers.title: Coix Seed Attenuates Acute Lung Injury via NLRP3 Signaling Pathway: Efficacy, Active Components, and Mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Coix seed is a medicinal and nutritional resource, but its protective effects against acute lung injury (ALI) remain unclear. This study investigated the efficacy, active components, and mechanisms of Coix seed extract (CSE) against ALI, focusing on the NLRP3 signaling pathway. The therapeutic efficacy of CSE was evaluated in a murine model of ALI. Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry identified 32 components in CSE, which were then analyzed via network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations for target prediction and drug-likeness evaluation. In vivo effects on
papers.summary: This study shows that Coix seed extract reduces acute lung injury in mice, with effects linked to the NLRP3 inflammasome signaling pathway. Using LC-MS, network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics, the authors identified 32 components and predicted their targets, suggesting multi-component anti-inflammatory mechanisms.

papers.title: SMILES2Docking: An Open-Source Desktop Workflow for Ligand Ionization, Stereochemistry-Aware Preparation and Semi-Empirical 3D Refinement.
papers.abstract: SMILES2Docking converts spreadsheet-based SMILES libraries into docking-ready 3D ligands through a single, configurable pipeline. Salt and coformer removal, a three-mode stereocenter policy, prediction of the dominant protonation state with a graph neural network pKa model (MolGpKa) refined by iterative titration, distance-geometry embedding with RDKit, a molecular-mechanics optimization cascade, and an optional semi-empirical refinement under an implicit solvation model are combined in one tool, with records processed either sequentially or distributed across CPU cores. Users select among per
papers.summary: SMILES2Docking is an open-source desktop workflow that converts spreadsheet-based SMILES libraries into docking-ready 3D ligands through a single configurable pipeline. It combines salt removal, stereocenter handling, GNN-based pKa prediction (MolGpKa), distance-geometry embedding, molecular mechanics optimization, and optional semi-empirical refinement with implicit solvation. The tool supports parallel processing across CPU cores for efficient large-scale ligand preparation.

papers.title: From wireframes to immersive reality: a historical perspective on molecular visualization software.
papers.abstract: The evolution of molecular visualization software represents a pivotal yet often underappreciated dimension of computational structural biology and bioinformatics. As the scale and complexity of structural datasets increase, spanning from cryo-electron microscopy reconstructions to proteome-wide AI-predicted models, visualization tools have become essential for data interpretation, hypothesis generation, and effective scientific communication. Widely used platforms such as PyMOL, UCSF Chimera, and emerging virtual reality environments reflect decades of progressive innovation driven by advance
papers.summary: This review traces the historical evolution of molecular visualization software, from early wireframe representations to modern immersive virtual reality environments. It highlights how tools like PyMOL and UCSF Chimera have become essential for interpreting increasingly complex structural data, including cryo-EM reconstructions and AI-predicted proteome-scale models. The paper argues that visualization is a pivotal but underappreciated driver of progress in computational structural biology.

papers.title: [Effects of astragaloside Ⅰ on full-thickness skin defects in diabetic rats and its underlying mechanism].
papers.abstract: Objective: To investigate the effects of astragaloside Ⅰ (AS-Ⅰ) on full-thickness skin defects in diabetic rats and its underlying mechanism. Methods: This study was an experimental study with grouped design and repeated measures design. Twenty-four male Sprague-Dawley rats aged 6-8 weeks were divided into control group (n=6) and modeling group (n=18) using a random number table method (the same grouping method was used throughout). After successful induction of diabetes mellitus, the modeling group was further divided into model group, low-dose AS-Ⅰ group, and high-dose AS-Ⅰ group, with 6 rat
papers.journal: Zhonghua shao shang yu chuang mian xiu fu za zhi
papers.summary: This study investigated whether astragaloside I (AS-I), a compound derived from the traditional Chinese herb Astragalus, can promote healing of full-thickness skin wounds in diabetic rats. Diabetic rats with skin defects were treated with low or high doses of AS-I, and healing outcomes and underlying molecular mechanisms were assessed. The findings suggest AS-I may accelerate wound healing in diabetes, potentially offering a therapeutic avenue for diabetic wound complications.

papers.title: Development and evaluation of a multi-epitope subunit vaccine against Salmonella Enteritidis infection.
papers.abstract: Salmonella Enteritidis (S. Enteritidis) is a major pathogen causing foodborne diseases worldwide, posing a serious threat to public health security and the sustainable development of the poultry industry. To overcome the limitations of conventional vaccines in terms of efficacy, safety, and cross-protection, a novel multi-epitope subunit vaccine (SEMV) was designed and constructed using an immunoinformatics-based strategy. Through systematic screening of epitopes from key immunogenic proteins of S. Enteritidis (SseB, SipC, OmpD and TolC), a total of 8 B-cell epitopes, 4 MHC-I-restricted epitop
papers.summary: This study designed a multi-epitope subunit vaccine against Salmonella Enteritidis using immunoinformatics, combining B-cell and MHC-I epitopes from four immunogenic proteins (SseB, SipC, OmpD, TolC). The construct was evaluated for immunogenicity and safety, aiming to overcome limitations of conventional vaccines in efficacy and cross-protection.

papers.title: Unveiling the molecular toxicity of plasticizers derived from microplastics (DMP and DEP) in diabetic kidney disease: integrative insights from network toxicology and multi-omics analysis.
papers.abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a prevalent microvascular complication with limited therapeutic options. This study aimed to identify biomarkers associated with microplastic-associated plasticizers in DKD and to explore their potential molecular mechanisms.
papers.summary: This study investigates how microplastic-derived plasticizers (DMP and DEP) may contribute to diabetic kidney disease by combining network toxicology with multi-omics data analysis. The authors identify candidate biomarkers and propose molecular mechanisms linking plasticizer exposure to DKD pathology. The work is exploratory and integrative, aiming to generate hypotheses rather than confirm causal relationships.

papers.title: Multiscale mechanistic modeling for the rational design of novel dual-target candidates against acetylcholinesterase and NADPH oxidase: an advanced computational study.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease is a complex neurodegenerative illness strongly associated with oxidative stress, which requires immediate intervention for therapeutic agents with potent antioxidant properties.
papers.summary: This computational study uses multiscale mechanistic modeling to rationally design dual-target drug candidates that inhibit both acetylcholinesterase and NADPH oxidase, two enzymes implicated in Alzheimer's disease pathology. The approach combines molecular modeling techniques to identify compounds with simultaneous antioxidant and cholinergic activity, offering a potential strategy for more effective Alzheimer's therapeutics.

papers.title: Repurposing MK0873 as a non-covalent hTERT-Targeting compound: a proof of concept study.
papers.abstract: Telomerase is a key regulator of both cellular immortality and aging, making it an attractive target for cancer therapy and age associated pathologies. Its clinical exploitation has been limited by structural complexity and challenges in achieving specificity. Recent structural insights into human telomerase reverse transcriptase (hTERT) have enabled the identification of selective inhibitors. Here, we repurposed MK0873, a PDE4 inhibitor previously evaluated in Phase II clinical trials for rheumatoid arthritis and COPD, as a non covalent telomerase targeting agent. In silico docking and molecu
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study repurposes MK0873, a PDE4 inhibitor previously tested in Phase II trials for inflammatory diseases, as a non-covalent inhibitor of human telomerase (hTERT) using in silico docking and molecular dynamics simulations. The work suggests a potential shortcut to telomerase-targeted therapies by leveraging an existing clinical-stage drug, though experimental validation of telomerase inhibition and anti-cancer/anti-aging effects remains to be demonstrated.

papers.title: Targeting IDH-driven Oncometabolism in glioblastoma: a computational approach for the identification of potential inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a malignant brain tumor frequently driven by mutations in isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH1 and IDH2) enzymes, which promote neomorphic synthesis of the oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate (2-HG) and subsequent metabolic dysfunction. Although these mutations are associated with different clinical outcomes, therapeutic intervention remains challenging due to tumor heterogeneity, cellular plasticity, restricted blood-brain barrier permeability, drug efflux mechanisms, and effective DNA repair pathways. Therefore, this study aims to identify selective inhibitors of mutant IDH pro
papers.summary: This study uses computational drug discovery methods to identify potential selective inhibitors of mutant IDH1 and IDH2 enzymes, which drive glioblastoma through production of the oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate. The work targets a well-known cancer metabolic vulnerability, though the abstract is truncated and does not report specific compounds or experimental validation.

papers.title: Elucidating adverse drug reactions and underlying molecular mechanisms of ivermectin through pharmacovigilance and multi-omics analysis.
papers.abstract: The comprehensive safety profile and underlying molecular mechanisms of ivermectin-associated adverse drug reactions (ADRs) remain to be fully elucidated.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study combines pharmacovigilance data with multi-omics analyses to characterize adverse drug reactions associated with ivermectin and to uncover their underlying molecular mechanisms. By integrating real-world safety reports with molecular profiling, the authors aim to provide a more comprehensive safety profile for this widely used antiparasitic drug.

papers.title: Deep DNA and protein level feature integration for robust clinical variant interpretation using probabilistic gradient boosting.
papers.abstract: A major challenge in clinical genomics is to classify genetic variations correctly, since it directly affects disease diagnosis and personal care. The existing methods tend to be based on the combination of different factors, such as protein structure, population frequencies, phenotypic annotations, and sequence conservation. Nevertheless, these methods often cannot be used to achieve the necessary interpretability, quantify uncertainty, and address rare cases. This paper presents a probabilistic gradient boosting model on variant pathogenicity prediction. The suggested framework applies biolo
papers.summary: This paper introduces a probabilistic gradient boosting model that integrates DNA- and protein-level features to improve clinical variant pathogenicity prediction. The approach aims to provide better interpretability and uncertainty quantification than existing multi-factor methods, particularly for rare variants.

papers.title: Anti-Lung Cancer Agent Discovery and Development: A Review of Cross-Platform Correlation Across in silico, Network Pharmacology, in vitro, and in vivo Assessments.
papers.abstract: Lung cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, highlighting the urgent need for more effective and clinically translatable therapeutic agents. In recent years, drug discovery strategies integrating computational modeling with experimental validation have gained increasing attention; however, their predictive consistency across biological scales remains a critical challenge. This review systematically synthesises evidence from eleven primary studies that evaluated anti-lung cancer agents across computational, cellular, and organism-level platforms within a
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence from eleven primary studies that evaluated anti-lung cancer agents across computational, network pharmacology, in vitro, and in vivo platforms, focusing on how well predictions from one scale translate to another. It highlights that cross-platform predictive consistency remains a critical challenge in integrated drug discovery pipelines. The work provides a framework for assessing the reliability of multi-scale anti-lung cancer agent evaluation.

papers.title: Environmental PFOA exposure and the risk of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: An integrated computational toxicology and multi-omics study.
papers.abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), a pervasive environmental pollutant, has been implicated in hepatic injury and metabolic dysfunction. However, its role as an environmental risk factor in the pathogenesis of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD) remains incompletely understood, particularly from a systems biology perspective.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether environmental exposure to PFOA contributes to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) using an integrated computational toxicology and multi-omics approach. By combining toxicological prediction tools with multi-omics data, the authors identify potential molecular pathways and mechanisms linking PFOA exposure to MASLD pathogenesis from a systems biology perspective.

papers.title: Repurposing of lansoprazole and nitazoxanide as NR2F2 inhibitors in the gastric cancer cell line GCIY: computational insights and siRNA-mediated in vitro tests.
papers.abstract: Nuclear receptors (NRs) are a superfamily of ligand-activated transcription factors that mediate the cellular response to hormones, vitamins, and dietary lipids, thus orchestrating numerous physiological processes and influencing multiple disease states. Within this superfamily, NR2Fs, also known as Chicken Ovalbumin Upstream Promoter Transcription Factor (COUP-TF), are a family of nuclear orphan receptors, due to the lack of known endogenous ligands. Among them, NR2F2 transcription factor activities involve regulation of cell differentiation during organogenesis, maintenance of adult tissue h
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and molecular dynamics to identify lansoprazole and nitazoxanide as potential inhibitors of the orphan nuclear receptor NR2F2 (COUP-TFII), followed by siRNA knockdown and in vitro assays in the gastric cancer cell line GCIY to test the effects. The findings suggest these FDA-approved drugs could be repurposed to target NR2F2-driven pathways in gastric cancer, though validation remains preliminary.

papers.title: Naringenin as a dual-target modulator of RAGE-NF-κB signaling and Aβ fibrillization in Alzheimer's disease: integrated computational and experimental analyses.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a complex neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the accumulation and aggregation of β-amyloid (Aβ) and chronic neuroinflammation mediated by the receptor for advanced glycation end products (RAGE). Current therapeutic candidates targeting RAGE signaling or Aβ aggregation continue to face challenges, including off-target toxicity, poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, and limited multi-target efficacy.
papers.summary: This study investigates naringenin, a natural flavonoid, as a potential dual-target treatment for Alzheimer's disease by modulating both RAGE-NF-κB neuroinflammatory signaling and Aβ fibrillization. Using integrated computational and experimental approaches, the authors identify naringenin as a compound that can simultaneously interfere with two key pathological mechanisms. The findings suggest a multi-target strategy that may overcome limitations of current single-target AD therapies.

papers.title: Screening and characterization of pro-angiogenic peptides from Spirulina: computer simulation, experimental validation, and mechanistic insights.
papers.abstract: In this study, we identified novel pro-angiogenic peptides from Spirulina and elucidated their molecular mechanisms. Among the three fractions (A, B, and C) purified from the Spirulina protein extract by RP-HPLC, fraction B displayed the most potent pro-angiogenic activity. Through LC-MS/MS analysis, bioinformatics screening, and molecular docking, 20 candidate peptides were selected. In zebrafish models, five of these peptides, MFDCLR, MDMWGK, MNPGCR, MYDNFCK, and MPGLGR, significantly stimulated subintestinal vessel plexus (SIVP) growth and rescued intersegmental vessel (ISV) injury induced
papers.summary: This study identified novel pro-angiogenic peptides from Spirulina using a combination of computer simulation, molecular docking, and experimental validation. Fraction B from Spirulina protein extract showed the strongest pro-angiogenic activity, and five peptides (MFDCLR, MDMWGK, MNPGCR, MYDNFCK, MPGLGR) significantly promoted blood vessel growth in zebrafish models. The work provides mechanistic insights into how these peptides stimulate angiogenesis.

papers.title: Comparative and Subtractive Genomics Analysis of Multidrug-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae Strains for Novel Target Identification and Drug Repurposing Strategies.
papers.abstract: The rapid rise of multidrug-resistant (MDR) Klebsiella pneumoniae has created a major global health challenge due to the limited availability of conserved therapeutic targets effective across diverse resistant strains. In this study, an integrative computational target-discovery and drug-repurposing framework was applied to six clinically relevant K. pneumoniae strains. Comparative genomic analysis identified 3012 conserved genes, which were subsequently filtered to nine essential, non-host homologous proteins. Among these, three conserved cytoplasmic proteins (accD, cpxR, and mraZ) were prior
papers.summary: This study used comparative and subtractive genomics to identify conserved drug targets across six multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae strains, narrowing 3012 conserved genes down to nine essential, non-host-homologous proteins. Three cytoplasmic proteins (accD, cpxR, and mraZ) were prioritized as promising targets, and the authors applied drug repurposing strategies to find existing compounds that could inhibit them.

papers.title: Sesamum indicum-derived valdiate as a novel neuroprotective agent targeting PDE10A2 and SIRT1 in Huntington's disease.
papers.abstract: Huntington's disease is prevalent globally, with approximately 4.88 cases per 100,000 people, based on a systematic review and meta-analysis of 33 studies published between 2010 and 2022. Despite its significant prevalence, no proper treatment is available that directly addresses Huntington's disease. The existing treatments focus on symptom management, such as controlling chorea and psychiatric symptoms. The drugs used for this purpose may also cause side effects, including depression and Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary: This study identifies a compound derived from Sesamum indicum (sesame) that may act as a neuroprotective agent in Huntington's disease by targeting the proteins PDE10A2 and SIRT1. Using bioinformatics approaches, the authors propose this natural compound as a potential therapeutic lead, though experimental validation appears limited. The work highlights a plant-derived candidate for a disease that currently lacks treatments addressing its underlying causes.

papers.title: Large language models in bioinformatics: a comprehensive survey.
papers.abstract: The emergence of foundation models with trillion-level parameters has redefined the landscape of artificial intelligence. Various fields are developing their own large-scale models, which can solve many problems within the field and improve work efficiency. Biological large-scale models are a cross-disciplinary research field that combines mathematics, computer science, and biology, aiming to simulate and understand the structure, function, and dynamic changes of biological systems through the establishment of complex computational models. This field covers multiple levels such as biological p
papers.summary: This survey reviews the growing use of large language models (LLMs) and other foundation models in bioinformatics, covering how these trillion-parameter models are being adapted to biological problems. It organizes the cross-disciplinary landscape spanning mathematics, computer science, and biology, and discusses applications across multiple levels of biological organization. The paper serves as a broad overview of current capabilities and directions for LLMs in the life sciences.
